source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning
finding: LATS runs MCTS over agent actions. The LM is the agent, the value function and the reflector, and the tree uses real environment feedback. On HotPotQA it beat ReAct, Reflexion, ToT and RAP with GPT-3.5.
numbers: HotPotQA EM, GPT-3.5, acting: ReAct 0.32, ReAct best-of-k 0.38, Reflexion 0.51, ToT(ReAct) 0.39, RAP(ReAct) 0.54, LATS(ReAct) 0.63, LATS(n=10) 0.65, LATS(CoT+ReAct) 0.71. Reasoning only: CoT 0.34, CoT-SC 0.38, ToT 0.55, RAP 0.60, LATS(CoT) 0.62.
limits: Authors' own runs, GPT-3.5, subsets, no variance reported, no independent replication in the paper.
agent_relevance: S6 search gains most when the tree can use external observations; mix reasoning and acting traces in the value signal.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning
finding: On code, LATS with unit-test feedback set the HumanEval record. Gain over Reflexion is 1.7 points at GPT-4 and 15.7 at GPT-3.5.
numbers: HumanEval pass@1 GPT-4: base 80.1, Reflexion 91.0, LATS 92.7. GPT-3.5: CoT 46.9, ReAct 56.9, Reflexion 68.1, ToT 54.4, RAP 63.1, LATS 83.8. MBPP GPT-3.5: CoT 54.9, ReAct 67.0, Reflexion 70.0, ToT 65.8, RAP 71.4, LATS 81.1.
limits: Search uses model-written tests; real tests only at final scoring. The GPT-4 gain over a plain reflection loop is small.
agent_relevance: Executable feedback is the strongest signal for S6; tree search adds little over a reflection loop when the base model is strong.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning
finding: On WebShop LATS raised the score a lot over Reflexion but the success rate only a little.
numbers: WebShop GPT-3.5 score/SR: ReAct 53.8/28.0, ReAct best-of-k 59.1/32.0, Reflexion 64.2/35.0, LATS 75.9/38.0, IL 59.9/29.1, IL+RL 62.4/28.7.
limits: SR gain over Reflexion is 3 points; score gain is 11.7. Single run.
agent_relevance: Partial-credit scores can hide small gains in strict success.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning
finding: Ablations: the LM value function is the load-bearing part, reflection adds about 5 points, MCTS beats DFS.
numbers: HotPotQA EM: LATS(ReAct) 0.63; no reflection 0.58; DFS 0.42; no LM heuristic 0.37; ToT(ReAct) 0.39; RAP(ReAct) 0.54. Game of 24 GPT-3.5: CoT 0.08, Reflexion 0.12, ToT 0.20, RAP 0.40, LATS 0.44.
limits: HotPotQA ablations, one seed.
agent_relevance: Invest in the value judge first; reflection second.

source: Zhou et al. (2023) Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning, Acting and Planning
finding: LATS costs more than ReAct but fewer nodes than ToT or RAP per success. Authors state two limits: compute cost and the need to revert the environment to earlier states.
limits: Node counts count successful runs only. About 170k tokens per success.
agent_relevance: The agent needs checkpoint and undo to run real tree search.

source: Koh, McAleer, Fried, Salakhutdinov (2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Best-first search in real web environments lifts GPT-4o and Llama-3 agents on VisualWebArena and WebArena.
numbers: VWA: GPT-4o+SoM 18.9% to 26.4% (+39.7% relative). WebArena GPT-4o 15.0% to 19.2% (+28.0%). Llama-3-70B caption agent on VWA 7.6% to 16.7% (+119.7%); text Llama-3 on WebArena 7.6% to 10.1% (+32.3%). Humans: 78% WA, 89% VWA.
limits: Absolute success remains under 27%. Gains are large relative to weak baselines.
agent_relevance: Search helps weak and mid agents most; it does not close the gap to humans.

source: Koh et al. (2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Success rises with search budget, depth and breadth. Even small search helps. Both depth and breadth must grow.
limits: 200-task subset, one model.
agent_relevance: Give S6 a small default budget and raise it on medium-difficulty problems.

source: Koh et al. (2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: The value function is the bottleneck. A ground-truth reward beats the best LM value function by 6.5 points. Self-consistency in the value call is essential.
numbers: Value function (VWA subset): none 24.5%; LLaVA-34B with SC n=20 30.0%; GPT-4o no SC 28.5%; GPT-4o SC n=5 32.5%; SC n=20 37.0%; ground truth 43.5%.
limits: SC n=20 multiplies value-call cost about 20 times.
agent_relevance: Sample the judge several times and average; a better judge beats a bigger tree.

source: Koh et al. (2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Tree search beats trajectory-level re-ranking at equal compute, and gains are largest on medium-length tasks.
numbers: Re-ranking n whole trajectories plateaus near 30% at n=7; search c=5 beats it; c=20 gets 37.0%. By difficulty: easy 34.2% to 42.3% (+24%), medium 12.7% to 22.2% (+75%), hard 10.2% to 14.9% (+47%).
limits: Hard tasks may need deeper trees than d=5.
agent_relevance: Restarting from a mid-trajectory state beats sampling whole new attempts.

source: Chen et al. (2024) When is Tree Search Useful for LLM Planning? It Depends on the Discriminator
finding: Tree search, iterative correction and re-ranking all need a judge of about 90% accuracy to beat re-ranking. Current LLM judges fall short. Tree search was 10 to 20 times slower.
numbers: Simulated judges: tree search underperforms others at accuracy threshold 0.8 or less, then rises sharply at 0.9. Intrinsic judge accuracy: GPT-4-Turbo Spider 76.5, Bird 76.2, GSM8K 93.8; GPT-3.5 67.0/64.3/72.1.
limits: Text-to-SQL and GSM8K only; GSM8K tree search run on 100 of 500 items.
agent_relevance: Do not pay for tree search unless the judge is strong; measure judge accuracy first.

source: Chen et al. (2024) When is Tree Search Useful for LLM Planning?
finding: With real LLM judges, tree search gave no reliable gain over re-ranking. With naive judges it could not beat greedy decoding on Spider.
numbers: Spider greedy 62.3 vs best naive re-ranking 61.5. Bird greedy 16.0; GPT-3.5 tree search 14.0 vs re-ranking 18.0. GSM8K greedy 39.4; GPT-3.5 with environment observations: re-rank 47.6, iterative 48.4, tree search 51.0 (McNemar p>0.05). Oracle judge GSM8K: tree search 73.0 vs re-rank 64.1.
limits: On Bird with an oracle judge, iterative correction 32.7 beat tree search 29.3, which the authors tie to MCTS instability.
agent_relevance: Failed-replication style evidence: LATS-style gains are fragile when value is the model's own guess.

source: Chen et al. (2024) When is Tree Search Useful for LLM Planning?
finding: Giving the judge environment observations (executability check, execution result) raised discrimination accuracy sharply. This is how real feedback helps tree search.
numbers: CodeLlama-13B accuracy Spider 58.2 to 83.6, Bird 49.4 to 79.6, GSM8K 62.2 to 70.6 (up to +25.4, +30.2, +8.4). GPT-3.5 Spider 67.0 to 90.0, Bird 64.3 to 89.2.
limits: Gains on fixed pair sets; end-to-end gains were smaller.
agent_relevance: Feed execution results into the judge; cheapest lift for S6.

source: Huang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: Without oracle labels, self-correction (the reflection step in Reflexion and LATS) does not help and often hurts. Reported gains used oracle correctness labels.
numbers: GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1 (round 1) to 41.8 (round 2); GSM8K 75.9 to 75.1 to 74.7; HotpotQA 26.0 to 25.0 to 25.0. GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 91.5 to 89.0; HotpotQA 49.0 to 49.0 to 43.0. With oracle (GPT-3.5): GSM8K 84.3, CommonSenseQA 89.7, HotpotQA 29.0.
limits: Tests plain self-correction prompts, not search. Some prior gains came from weak first-round prompts.
agent_relevance: Tie every reflection to a real check, never to self-judgement alone.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
finding: Reflexion stores a verbal lesson after each failed trial and retries; this is the reflection part inside LATS. It uses a binary environment signal or a simple heuristic.
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 tasks in 12 trials; ReAct alone stalled between trials 6 and 7. HumanEval Python pass@1 91.0 vs GPT-4 80.1. MBPP Python 77.1 vs 80.1 (worse). Rust HumanEval 68.0 vs 60.0. LeetcodeHard 15.0 vs 7.5.
limits: Did not beat GPT-4 base on MBPP Python. Needs test suites or heuristics.
agent_relevance: Reflection memory with outside signals is the cheap baseline LATS must beat.

source: Hao et al. (2023) Reasoning with Language Model is Planning with World Model (RAP)
finding: RAP uses the LM as its own world model and runs MCTS over reasoning steps, with no environment. It is LATS's closest search baseline.
numbers: Blocksworld LLaMA-33B success 2/4/6-step: CoT 0.17/0.02/0.00; RAP(10) 1.00/0.86/0.26; RAP(20) 1.00/0.88/0.42; GPT-4 CoT 0.50/0.63/0.40. Average RAP success 64%.
limits: Simulated outcomes err at longer horizons (6-step 26% to 42%). Test cases: 30, 57, 114.
agent_relevance: Real feedback beats simulated; LATS beat RAP by 9 points on HotPotQA acting.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) Accessing GPT-4 level Mathematical Olympiad Solutions via Monte Carlo Tree Self-refine (MCTSr)
finding: MCTS where each node is a refined answer scored by self-rating. Gains rise with rollouts on easy sets and stall on hard ones.
numbers: LLaMA-3 8B GSM8K: zero-shot CoT 74.07%, one self-refine 86.96%, MCTSr 4 rollouts 93.03%, 8 rollouts 96.66%. GSM-Hard: 25.47%, 33.36%, 39.88%, 45.49%.
limits: Technical report, self-rating reward, authors note a ceiling on hard sets.
agent_relevance: Self-scored search may look strong on easy math; treat as an upper bound.

source: Zhang et al. (2024) ReST-MCTS*: LLM Self-Training via Process Reward Guided Tree Search
finding: A learned process reward guides MCTS and then trains the policy. At equal token budget, the first iteration did not fully beat self-consistency.
numbers: MATH same budget: ReST-MCTS* iteration 1 did not completely surpass Self-Consistency; after more self-training it reached 48.5% vs SC 42.5%.
limits: Needs a trained value model; MATH and SciBench only.
agent_relevance: With a prompted (untrained) value, expect near parity with self-consistency.

source: Wu et al. (2024) Inference Scaling Laws: An Empirical Analysis of Compute-Optimal Inference for LLM Problem-Solving
finding: MCTS is not compute-efficient against sampling plus voting. Their simpler tree search (REBASE) beat MCTS and sampling. A small model with good search beat a larger model.
numbers: Llemma-7B with REBASE matches Llemma-34B with about 2x fewer FLOPs on MATH500 and GSM8K, and beats Llemma-34B with majority voting at all budgets. MCTS often needs dozens of times more generated tokens.
limits: Math only; PRM-based value; MCTS is the authors' version, not LATS.
agent_relevance: Count tokens: MCTS spends many tokens on rollouts that never enter the answer.

source: Snell et al. (2024) Scaling LLM Test-Time Compute Optimally can be More Effective than Scaling Model Parameters
finding: Search against a process reward model: lookahead (a special case of MCTS) generally underperformed beam search and best-of-N at equal generations. The best method depends on question difficulty.
numbers: Compute-optimal allocation gave over 4x efficiency vs best-of-N. With FLOPs matched, a smaller model plus test-time compute beat a 14x larger model on easy and medium questions. Beam search over-optimizes on easy questions at high budgets and falls below best-of-N.
limits: MATH, PaLM 2, trained PRM. Gains shrink on the hardest questions.
agent_relevance: Choose search depth by difficulty; skip search on easy items.

source: Brown et al. (2024) Large Language Monkeys: Scaling Inference Compute with Repeated Sampling
finding: Repeated sampling with an automatic verifier is a strong baseline for tree search. Coverage rises log-linearly with samples; voting and reward-model selection plateau.
numbers: SWE-bench Lite, DeepSeek-Coder-V2: 15.9% at 1 sample to 56% at 250 samples, above the 43% single-sample SOTA.
limits: Needs a reliable verifier such as tests.
agent_relevance: Compare any LATS result with the same number of independent samples and the same verifier.

source: Antoniades et al. (2025) SWE-Search: Enhancing Software Agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search and Iterative Refinement
finding: MCTS with a hybrid LM value (number plus written feedback) and a debate-based discriminator on SWE-bench Lite gave 23% mean relative gain across five models.
numbers: Resolve rate, Moatless-Adapted to SWE-Search: GPT-4o 25.7 to 31.0, GPT-4o-mini 13.0 to 17.0, Qwen2.5-72B 18.0 to 24.7, DeepSeek-V2.5 16.3 to 21.0, Llama-3.1-70B 13.6 to 17.7. Value function picks the right solution 73% of the time; discriminator 84%.
limits: Cost for GPT-4o rose from $40.86 to $576.00, about 14 times. Absolute gains are 4 to 7 points.
agent_relevance: A separate judge stage and written feedback both added accuracy; cost is high.

source: Putta et al. (2024) Agent Q: Advanced Reasoning and Learning for Autonomous AI Agents
finding: MCTS with an AI critic ranking actions, plus DPO training on the search tree. Test-time MCTS added much on top of the trained agent.
numbers: WebShop: DPO 31.3%, RFT 40.6%, MCTS on base 48.4%, Agent Q + MCTS 50.5% vs average human 50.0%. Real OpenTable booking, Llama-3 70B: zero-shot 18.6%, RFT 67.2%, Agent Q 81.7%, Agent Q + MCTS 95.4%.
limits: Needs training; the critic is the same base LLM; one custom real-world task.
agent_relevance: With no training, expect less than these numbers.

source: Cross-reading of the machine evidence in this file (LATS, Chen, Koh, Wu, Snell, Brown, SWE-Search)
finding: Tree search over LLM agents helps when the signal is external (tests, execution, environment), the judge is strong or sampled several times, and the environment can be reverted. It does not help, or is not compute-efficient, when the signal is the model's own opinion.
numbers: LATS +1.7 HumanEval over Reflexion at GPT-4; Chen: no significant gain below about 90% judge accuracy; Wu: MCTS needs dozens of times more tokens; SWE-Search about 14x cost for +5.3 points on GPT-4o.
limits: Cross-paper comparison; budgets and benchmarks differ.
agent_relevance: S6: use tree-style retries only with a real checker, a revert step and a stated budget; otherwise best-of-N plus checker.

source: Koh et al. (2025) Tree Search for Language Model Agents
finding: Baseline web agents commonly fail by compounding error: one early wrong action ruins the run. Search lets the agent back out and try a different branch.
numbers: Qualitative case studies (for example VWA classifieds task 48) where greedy first-sample actions fail and search finds a working path; ground-truth value reaches 43.5% vs 37.0% for LM value.
limits: Case studies are picked examples. Destructive actions in live sites limit trajectory-level retries.
agent_relevance: Backtracking to a checkpoint is the benefit; keep an undo log in S6.

source: Huang et al. (2023) Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
finding: The oracle-label setting leaks the answer: the loop stops when the answer is right and only changes wrong ones. That explains big gains in earlier reflection papers.
numbers: GPT-4 with oracle: GSM8K 95.5 to 97.5, CommonSenseQA 82.0 to 85.5, HotpotQA 49.0 to 59.0. GPT-3.5 with oracle: GSM8K 75.9 to 84.3.
limits: Only prompt-based self-correction was tested, not search with execution feedback.
agent_relevance: Check whether a LATS-style result used ground-truth stops; ours must not.
